items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And we’ll get — who do you want to get? We’ll get Johnny Mandel, we’ll get Ralph Burns. ... And there’s Clare Fischer, and there’s John Clayton, there’s Patrick Williams, there’s Johnny Mandel, there’s Michel Legrand and his entire French orchestra who just came in off a plane to play a concert... B

ctx.x: This will only take 25 minutes. Talk about blessed, I mean everywhere along the way, something good happened. And so Chesky Records makes a record of Johnny Frigo and me and Bucky, Ron Carter or Michael Moore and Butch Miles playing with Johnny © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

Frigo, you know, a violin player. And we all sat around the mic and play acoustic jazz, and then Chesky, David and Norman Chesky, the had just started the label. They go like, “We’re looking for a male singer, you know any male singers who could be on—” I said “Why don’t you come hear my group?” So they’d come to the thing, they’d hear my trio up at Jay’s when it used to be a great club here in New York, and I finished the set and David Chesky says, “well we’re going to get Milt Hinton and Clark Terry and your…

items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...I’m seeing Don Sebesky, Pat Williams, Clare Fisher. [INTERVIEWEE] Johnny Mandel.

ctx.x: Yeah. I mean I just heard it the way I heard it, from listening to other guys play. I mean once the hand starts to know where all the little triads were, then you’d start to find other notes and you’d go ah, I see where that’s at. And there were two licks my father showed me [scats]. That was one of them. And there’s [scats], that was, like so on G it would be [scats]. At any rate, well it’s close, I mean that was it. And he said, “ah, you can play that on a two-five.” Over there, when he got to two-five, which…
Wow. You’ve had, it seems like, pretty good success with record label support. I was looking at your Christmas album and I’m seeing Don Sebesky, Pat Williams, Clare Fisher.
